reason: Nearly all the weight is on bills about who controls judicial selection. Row 1 (57.5 of 98) is the 2023 bill that changes the composition of the Judicial Selection Committee so that elected officials hold the majority. Rows 5-7, 9, 10 and 12 also change the committee's composition or its voting majority. Row 8 does the same for the rabbinical judges committee and carries little weight. Row 3 (the Knesset elects the Supreme Court president) and row 4 (how the president is appointed) are about elected versus professional control of top judicial posts, and the statement's price ('elected officials have little say over who becomes a judge') covers them. Row 2 (a Constitutional Court) is the only weighty bill outside a strict 'committee' reading, but its stated label is about political appointment of judges, so it fits the same question. The statement asks one idea, names the price, has 25 words and an agree key (less political influence) that matches the label direction.
